statement: NVIDIA's DSX MaxLPS raises AI-factory performance per watt by roughly 1.5x on GB200 NVL72 and 1.3-1.4x on Vera Rubin NVL72 within a fixed power budget.
why: Site power, not silicon, is the binding constraint on AI factory build-out, so a step up in throughput per watt converts stranded power headroom into deployable accelerator capacity.

impact.mechanism: Chip, thermal, system and software techniques cut rack power (GB200 NVL72 from 125 kW to 90 kW; Vera Rubin NVL72 from 136 kW to 101 kW), so the same megawatts host more racks and more GPUs.

evidence.excerpt: performance per watt improves approximately 1.5x on GB200 NVL72 and 1.3-1.4x on Vera Rubin NVL72.

confidence.basis: Vendor-authored secondary blog post from a single publisher; figures are NVIDIA's own and not independently corroborated.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: developer.nvidia.com
